street.title: The street: twelve Buys, targets ₹195-235 (median ₹210), on 22-25x FY28E hotel EBITDA plus the Colombo apartments and cash
street.methodText: Every house that discloses a method values ITC Hotels on **EV/EBITDA of the hotel business** on FY28E (some on Dec-27E or Mar-28E), and the sum-of-the-parts versions add Sapphire Residences at about 1x its net asset value plus net cash: ICICI Direct 22x FY28E (₹1,936 cr EBITDA, Sapphire NAV ₹1,175 cr), Choice 22x FY28E hospitality EBITDA with the apartments at 0x, Jefferies and Nomura 23x FY28E (Nomura: a ~10% discount to IHCL), JM Financial 25x Mar-28E, ICICI Securities 25x Dec-27E (May note). We do the same on Sep-28E EBITDA, the 12-month-forward year the market will look at in September 2027.

street.text: Twelve brokers had a standing view on 30-Sep-2026, all Buy or Outperform where a rating is stated, with targets of ₹195-235 (median ₹210, mean ~₹213) against a price of ₹164. After the Q1FY27 results (16-Jul-2026) ICICI Securities raised its target to ₹235, Choice to ₹210 (from ₹190), ICICI Direct kept ₹220 (22x FY28E), Macquarie cut to ₹210 (from ₹220); Investec started at ₹201 (16-Sep) and Jefferies reiterated ₹210 on 23x FY28E (22-Sep). The May-2026 notes after the West Asia shock (Nomura ₹195, Elara ₹197, PhillipCapital ₹200, JM ₹225, Ambit ₹225) still stand. The pattern is telling: targets were cut from ₹230-253 in January (Nomura, JM, Elara) to ~₹195-235, multiples from 25-30x to 22-25x, yet the stock fell further. Bulls argue the luxury hotels are irreplaceable, the managed pipeline lifts margins and returns, and Colombo is now profitable. No note we found adjusted for the low return on capital or the BAT overhang.

ownership.holdersAsOf: Mar-2026 (AR FY26) and Dec-2025 shareholding pattern
ownership.text: ITC Ltd holds 39.85% (83 cr shares) and is the only promoter. At the demerger BAT's entities received ~15.3% (pro rata to their ITC stake). On 5-Dec-2025 BAT sold ~9% (18.75 cr shares at an average ₹205.65, ~₹3,856 cr) to buyers including ADIA, HCL Capital, Nippon India MF and Vanguard, calling the stake 'not a strategic holding'; it kept 6.28% through Tobacco Manufacturers (India), and we found no further sale by 30-Sep-2026. That is why the FII share fell from 25.5% (Sep-25) to 16.1% (Dec-25) and 11.6% (Jun-26), while the 'public' line (which includes BAT's residual stake and HCL Capital) rose to 24.5%. LIC (8.70%) and SUUTI (4.68%) came with their ITC holdings. 22.9 lakh shareholders at Jun-2026, most of them small ITC holders who received shares in the demerger.

critiques: Growth is ordinary: hotels grew 10% in FY26 and Q1FY27, room rates only 6% and 4%; the street's FY28E revenue (+15-16% in ICICI Direct and Choice) needs a big step-up.
Returns are low: ROE ~7% and pre-tax ROCE ~11% on ₹11,658 cr of equity; the cash pile earns ~7% and dilutes returns further.
The apartment sales in Colombo flatter FY26 growth (₹211 cr revenue) and are lumpy (₹38 cr in Q1FY27); Sri Lankan taxes slowed sales and the currency hits book value.
Overhang: BAT still holds 6.28% and calls it non-strategic; the stock fell 19% in 2026 to 30-Sep.
Fee business is small: ₹173 cr of fees vs IHCL's ₹685 cr; most managed hotels are midscale in smaller cities.
Disclosure: no earnings calls and no numerical guidance, so the street relies on decks and the AGM.

Bull case: irreplaceable city luxury hotels, a 33-37% RevPAR premium, ~₹3,175 cr of net cash plus ~₹1,240 cr of apartments to sell (~13% of the market value together), and an asset-light pipeline that lifts margins.
